speaker: Patient
text: 57-year-old male. The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. He mentions that his legs have been chronically swollen for over 10 years and that his mother and brother had similar leg problems. He had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years ago but has no other significant past medical history.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Lipodermatosclerosis secondary to chronic venous insufficiency.

Given the 6-month non-healing wound on the right lower leg, 10-year history of bilateral leg swelling, strong family history, and prior DVT, the clinical picture strongly suggests venous stasis. To confirm the diagnosis and assess the extent of the issue, I will now request your leg imaging results. REQUEST IMAGES: Venous Ultrasound
